extra.message: User-controlled 'format' (from POST /export/renewals/convert body) is interpolated directly into a shell command executed via execSync: `pandoc ${tmpInput} -f csv -t ${format} -o ${tmpOutput}`. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters to run arbitrary OS commands (RCE). Contrast with convertHealthReport which validates format against a whitelist and uses spawnSync without a shell.

saveRenewalSnapshot builds a file path from the user-supplied 'label' (POST /export/renewals/snapshot body) without sanitization: path.join(this.snapshotDir, `${label}.csv`). A label like '../../../../etc/cron.d/x' writes a file outside the intended directory (arbitrary file write). Contrast with saveEscalationsSnapshot which applies path.basename(label).

importDocumentFromExternalSource fetches an arbitrary URL supplied by the caller (x-document-source-url header, POST /documents/import-from-source) with no host/IP allow-list and writes the response to disk. This enables SSRF against internal services (e.g. cloud metadata endpoints) and arbitrary file download. Contrast with importDocumentFromApprovedRepository which validates the hostname against an allow-list.

The public /auth/register endpoint assigns the caller to an arbitrary organizationId taken from the request body with no check that the user is invited/authorized to join that organization. An attacker can self-register as a CUSTOMER_CONTACT of any organization (by its UUID) and then read that org's customer-visible documents, contacts, deals, escalations and API-key/webhook listings, which are all scoped by organizationId.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: findOne (used by GET /users/:id and GET /users/profile) returns the raw User entity directly. The User entity (user.entity.ts:37) has a passwordHash column with no @Exclude/select:false, so every response serializes the bcrypt password hash to the client. Combined with the lack of role restrictions on GET /users/:id, any authenticated user (including CUSTOMER_CONTACT) can enumerate other users and harvest password hashes for offline cracking. findAll() and getProfile() leak the same field.

recordKeyIssuanceForSupportTicket logs the full plaintext API key (issuedKey: rawKey) plus the whole apiKey entity and caller identity to application logs via logger.warn. This writes a long-lived credential to logs where it can be exfiltrated by anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: continueDocumentWorkflow redirects to a caller-supplied x-workflow-return-url header without validating it against an allow-list (res.redirect(workflowReturnUrl || '/documents')). This is an open redirect that can be abused for phishing/token theft. Contrast with continueEscalationWorkflow which validates against a fixed list of internal paths.

findStaffByEmail interpolates the caller-supplied email into an LDAP search filter without escaping: `(mail=${email})`. Special LDAP filter characters (e.g. *, (, )) allow injection of additional filter clauses. The value is not passed through escapeDirectoryFilterValue (which is only used by verifyEmployeeBadge).

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query (LDAP Injection)

extra.message: searchStaffDirectory interpolates the caller-supplied search term into an LDAP filter without escaping: `(cn=*${searchTerm}*)`. This allows LDAP filter injection, letting an attacker alter the search predicate (e.g. (cn=*)(|(cn=*)) style bypass or attribute enumeration).

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query (LDAP Injection)

extra.message: update() (PATCH /organizations/:id) modifies any organization by id without calling assertOrganizationAccess or applying a role guard, so any authenticated user (including CUSTOMER_CONTACT) can change another organization's name, renewal date and billing contact details (IDOR).

updateStatus() (PATCH /organizations/:id/status) changes an organization's status by id without calling assertOrganizationAccess, so any authenticated user can suspend/activate arbitrary organizations.

upload() stores the document against the organizationId taken from the multipart request body without verifying the uploading user belongs to that organization (contrast with contacts.create which validates organizationId). Any authenticated user can upload files into another organization's document library. importDocumentFromExternalSource and importDocumentFromApprovedRepository have the same missing check.

create() mints an API key for the organizationId in the request body without verifying the caller is authorized for that organization. A CUSTOMER_CONTACT (or any user) can create API keys for arbitrary organizations, and findAll() returns all API keys (including keyPrefix/keyHash) for those organizations.

create() registers a webhook for the organizationId in the request body without verifying the caller is authorized for that organization. Any authenticated user can create webhooks (with an arbitrary target URL) for another organization.

issueGoodwillCredit() updates an escalation by path id with no role check and no access check (it never calls findOne, unlike every other escalation method). Any authenticated user can POST /escalations/:id/goodwill-credit to set an arbitrary goodwill credit amount on any escalation; IssueCreditDto has no @Max cap.

previewCustomOrganizationNotice compiles a caller-supplied string as a Handlebars template (Handlebars.compile(customMessageTemplate)) with attacker-controlled context. This is server-side template injection; malicious template helpers/expressions are evaluated server-side.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The export endpoints (GET /export/renewals, /export/health, /export/escalations) have no @Roles restriction, so any authenticated user including CUSTOMER_CONTACT can export the renewal/billing/health/escalation data of ALL organizations, not just their own. Same applies to /export/renewals/labeled and the snapshot/convert POST endpoints.

update() mass-assigns the request body onto the deal (Object.assign(deal, updateDealDto)). UpdateDealDto includes 'stage', so PATCH /deals/:id lets a caller set any stage directly (e.g. CLOSED_WON/RENEWAL_PENDING), bypassing the ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS state machine enforced by the dedicated updateStage endpoint.

Hardcoded fallback JWT signing secret 'dev-secret-key-change-in-production' is used whenever JWT_SECRET is unset (also mirrored in jwt.strategy.ts:19). If deployed without the env var, anyone can forge valid JWT tokens and impersonate any user/role.

Database username/password default to 'postgres'/'postgres' when the environment variables are unset, providing well-known default credentials that allow full database access if the env is not configured.

CORS is configured with origin: true (reflects any Origin header) combined with credentials: true. This allows any website to make authenticated cross-origin requests using the user's session/token, enabling cross-site data theft.

The workspace_context session cookie is set without httpOnly, secure, or sameSite attributes (lines 29, 77 and 94), exposing the workspace session id to client-side script access and non-TLS transmission. The support_console_context cookie on line 45 correctly sets these flags.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: TypeORM synchronize: true is enabled, which auto-generates/destroys database schema from entities at runtime. If enabled in production this can cause destructive schema changes and data loss.

Seed data creates admin/manager/support/customer accounts with a well-known hardcoded password 'password123' (admin@example.com, manager@example.com, etc.). If the seed endpoint is ever run in a shared environment, these default credentials are trivially guessable.

checkTicketStatus (GET /escalations/portal/ticket-status) is @Public() and reveals a ticket's status and severity to anyone who supplies a valid ticket id and matching organization id, with no authentication or rate limiting, enabling enumeration of escalation records. The document checkDocumentAvailability endpoint has the same pattern.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
